task_message:
Case N44: segment the peripheral nerve sheath tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 141x141x82 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
I finished the case. Summary of what I did:

- Reviewed the volume in axial, coronal and sagittal contact sheets to locate the abnormality.
- Identified a large, spindle/oval-shaped, well-circumscribed T2 intermediate-to-hyperintense mass with a thin dark pseudocapsule and a bright "split-fat" rim at its poles — the dominant lesion in the extremity.
- Ruled out a bright tubular structure near the mass (vessel-like, ~20 mm long, 8 mm cross-section) that the model initially captured with a test point, and removed that attempt.
- Seeded the mass with positive points on the axial slice through its largest cross-section; the model produced a single-component 58.9 mL mask spanning axial 14–81, coronal 51–95, sagittal 46–100.
- Verified the outline against the lesion edge on axial slices at several levels (16, 31, 56, 70) and on coronal/sagittal planes; the boundary tracked the dark capsule with no leak into adjacent muscle.
- Checked the automatic candidates: C1–C3 were only the surrounding fat/normal tissue adjacent to the mass, so they were rejected.
- Saved the final mask with medium confidence (correct structure and clean boundary, but some uncertainty about the true superior extent where the lesion tapers toward the volume edge).
